answer: An agent economy can make identity cheap but influence scarce by requiring each account to post a bond that is slashed when its actions are proven fraudulent. Reputation then grows only through completed work that counterparties verify, and a new account cannot inherit another’s record. A sybil attacker may create a nebula of violet names, but each must lock real capital and earn trust separately; splitting identities therefore multiplies the bond and verification costs, while timber can serve as an ordinary traded good rather than a magical proof of personhood.
